---
title: "Edits"
subtitle: "How one contact state leads to the next: make, break, transfer, the rare compound edge, and the step chain."
lightbox: true
---

## The menu of edits

An **edit** changes a formation σ into a neighbor σ′. It is built from
elementary changes:

| Change | What it does | Example on the step |
|---|---|---|
| make(c) | adds a contact | make(s): push the box against the riser |
| break(c) | removes a contact | break(g<sub>v</sub>): lift the box's corner off the floor |
| transfer(c → d) | replaces a contact by one it contains, or the reverse | g → g<sub>v</sub>: the box starts to tip onto its corner; s<sub>v</sub> → t: it lands on the platform |
| transport | changes no contact; moves the pose toward the goal | slide the box along the floor |

**Containment** is Xiao and Ji's (Def. 8): d is contained in c when d's
features are c's or boundary elements of them. A transfer uses one-sided
containment (their cases 2–3): one feature stays, and the other is an edge
and one of its own end vertices. The box edge flat on the floor (g) shrinks
to its corner on the floor (g<sub>v</sub>); the box side on the platform (t)
shrinks to the box side on the step corner (s<sub>v</sub>). On the step
there are 56 such pairs among the 40 templates.

Break and transfer to a contained contact **relax**; make and transfer to a
containing contact **constrain**. Transport is offered only when the
current formation holds the box.

## When several contacts change at once

A set of elementary changes on different templates is an edge when:

- they all relax or all constrain (Xiao and Ji's containment between
  formations, Def. 9);
- the result is valid;
- no smaller nonempty subset of the changes gives a formation realized
  within ρ = 25 mm of the transition pose (the **local** rule, Decision 14:
  the question is asked where the change happens).

A single valid change is always an edge. A **compound** edge is a set of
changes that cannot be made one at a time. Moving the disk from −x<sub>B</sub>
to −z<sub>B</sub> is not one edge: breaking m<sub>x</sub> first leaves a valid
formation. The disk goes round the box corner in two transfers, through its
contact with the vertex.

The compound edge that matters on the step is the **pivot**:

{m<sub>x</sub>, g, s} ⇒ {m<sub>x</sub>, g<sub>v</sub>, s<sub>v</sub>}.

Tipping the box on its corner lifts its side off the riser at the same
instant. Both one-at-a-time intermediates, {m<sub>x</sub>, g<sub>v</sub>, s}
and {m<sub>x</sub>, g, s<sub>v</sub>}, are invalid (a box tilted on its corner
is not flush on the riser, and conversely). Under the local rule the step has
16 change sets: the pivot in the box's four orientations in the corner, in
both directions, and eight *rocking* moves, in which a box flush in the
floor–riser corner turns onto its far bottom vertex on the floor and its near
bottom vertex on the riser, and back. In the marking graph they give 92
compound edges. (The earlier global rule, "every proper subset is invalid
anywhere", admitted 136 on the valid formations, 40 of them joining formations
realized 85–184 mm apart, which no single motion connects.)

## The marking graph

The **marking graph** W has the valid, recognizable formations as vertices
and the edits as edges. A single change is an edge only if its two ends are
realized within ρ = 25 mm of each other at some transition pose, so W is a
neighbour graph in Xiao and Ji's sense (112 single changes whose ends lie
21–403 mm apart are dropped). On the step W has **328 vertices and 2,490
directed edges** (2,398 single, 92 compound), a mean out-degree of 7.6.
Checked exhaustively:

- every edge has its reverse;
- W is connected, and with at most k changes per edge the graph distance
  between σ and σ′ is at least |σ △ σ′|/(2k) (the symmetric difference) and,
  measured over all 107,584 ordered pairs, at most |σ △ σ′| + 2: a dropped
  transfer can force a detour of two edges.

## The step chain

With the disk free at the start, a plan for the step is the walk

{g} → {m<sub>x</sub>, g} → {m<sub>x</sub>, g, s} ⇒ {m<sub>x</sub>, g<sub>v</sub>, s<sub>v</sub>}
→ {m<sub>x</sub>, s<sub>v</sub>} → {m<sub>x</sub>, t} → {t} → {m<sub>z</sub>, t} → transport,

that is: make m<sub>x</sub>, make s, the pivot, break g<sub>v</sub>,
transfer s<sub>v</sub> → t, break m<sub>x</sub>, make m<sub>z</sub>, and
transport. This is the *direct* route, which lifts the floor corner with the
disk on −x<sub>B</sub>. The paper's running chain is the *indirect lift*, in
which the disk lets go after the pivot and lifts the box from its raised
underside, holding it at every instant
([Certifying a whole box](certificate.qmd#the-indirect-lift)).

![The box near the step corner, labeled by the recognizer. Left: resting on the corner alone, {s<sub>v</sub>}. Middle: landed with +x<sub>B</sub> on the platform and overhanging the corner. v<sub>S</sub> is the end of the platform edge the box rests on, so the box's contact with v<sub>S</sub> is not principal, and the formation is {t}. Right: clear of the corner, still {t}.](media/xj_landing.svg){.lightbox}

**Landing is a transfer.** Once +x<sub>B</sub> lies on the platform,
v<sub>S</sub> is a boundary element of the touching platform edge, so the
landed box realizes {t}, and sliding it clear of the corner changes no
contact. Support is unaffected: t's contact set ends at the corner, so the
landed box is held exactly when its center of mass is over the platform.

`Cand`, the candidate generator, offers every step of the chain from a pose
in its formation, provided the hold gate passes. Breaking g<sub>v</sub> needs
the box tilted well past 30° with the disk low on its face
([Certifying a whole box](certificate.qmd#the-pivot)).

## Reproduce

```bash
cd ~/repos/research/c-gnn && git switch phase1/planar && git pull && cd cmg
JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu PYTHONPATH=tests .venv314/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_planar_step2.py
JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu .venv314/bin/python <website>/research/nonprehensile/planar-build/scripts/03_xiao_ji.py <out dir>
```

`03_xiao_ji.py` prints the template and containment counts; it predates
validity from geometry. The counts of valid formations and edges come from the
validity builder, `reports/supporting_docs/validity/` in `c-gnn`.
